mission.brief: Explore a small Linux workspace as learner. Identify your starting directory (/home/learner), list its contents, enter Documents, read Documents/welcome.txt, and finish in /home/learner/Projects. Learn explains one command at a time; Challenge leaves the approach to you.
constraints: Four action objectives use successful simulated activity: pwd at /home/learner, ls of /home/learner, cd into Documents, and cat of Documents/welcome.txt. Actions may happen in any order; equivalent relative and absolute paths count.
The final-state objective checks your current directory at submission: /home/learner/Projects. Earlier action evidence remains recorded if you move elsewhere. No service needs starting.
The filesystem is read-only. Commands act immediately; there is no Apply step. Help and diagnostic checks do not complete action objectives.

Only help, pwd, ls [-l] [PATH], cd [PATH] and cat PATH are supported. Paths are case sensitive. cd without a path returns to /home/learner. No quotes, ~, wildcards, pipelines, substitutions or host commands.

/ is the virtual root. Going above it is rejected and leaves your directory unchanged (a simulation boundary, unlike a full Linux shell). Permissions are checked along the entire path; /root is private.

objectives.label: Action: identify the starting directory with pwd

hints: Use the prompt and pwd to orient yourself. Listing a folder shows what you can explore; listing alone does not enter it.
Relative paths start where you are; absolute paths start at /. A file can be read by either kind of path. .. refers to a parent directory.
Inspect /home/learner with pwd and ls, visit its Documents folder, read welcome.txt with cat, then end in /home/learner/Projects. Your action evidence survives moving between folders.

/home/learner/Documents/welcome.txt.content:
Welcome to your virtual Linux workspace!
Documents holds notes; Downloads holds incoming files.
Projects is where you will finish this exercise.
All files here belong to the simulation.

/etc/motd.content: Learning Lab: a small simulated filesystem.

/root/private.txt.content: This virtual file is reserved for the simulated root user.

lesson.goal: Explore your home folder, visit Documents and read welcome.txt, then finish in Projects. Lab details explains each objective.

steps.explanation: pwd means print working directory. It tells you where you are now.
ls lists the contents of a directory. Without a path, it lists where you are now.
steps.expected: Documents, Downloads and Projects appear as virtual paths.

steps.explanation: cd changes directory. A relative path starts from your current directory.
cat displays a text file. Read this short note to learn what these folders are for.
steps.expected: A welcome note describing Documents, Downloads and Projects.

steps.explanation: A path beginning with / is absolute: it works from any current directory.
steps.expected: The prompt ends in /home/learner/Projects. Submit to record your result.
